messages:
Ravi: quick note from today's QA pass on the Console toolbar (compact mode). noticed icon-only buttons have very thin focus outlines and some color combos fall below 3:1 contrast in hover state.
Nora: thanks. which page and which buttons? screenshots?
Ravi: /console -> model details -> top toolbar (edit, deploy, rotate key). compact toolbar uses 24px icons, background is transparent, hover uses subtle gray. attached screenshot in ticket but tl;dr: default focus ring is 1px and color is #9aa0a6 which fails WCAG for focus indicator in several themes.
Priya: oof. keyboard users rely on visible focus. we should follow focus-visible pattern and ensure at least 3:1 contrast for focus outline against background per WCAG 2.1? iirc focus indicator contrast guidance is 3:1 non-text.
Dylan: correct, for non-text contrast (UI components) aim for 3:1 when possible. recommended approach: increase thickness + choose color token that meets contrast in both light and dark themes, or use an overlay ring with background-dim.
Ravi: repro steps: tab into compact toolbar buttons (keyboard only), observe thin dashed focus, on hover state the icon color shifts to #6b7280 which is borderline against white in light theme. in dark theme some icons are fine but outline gets lost over gradients.
Nora: can we add `:focus-visible` rules and a fallback for UA focus on older browsers? also consider `outline-offset` so ring doesn't overlap the icon.
Priya: proposed CSS snippet:
```
.icon-btn:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid var(--focus-accent);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  border-radius: 6px; /* match token */
}
@media (prefers-contrast: more) {
  .icon-btn:focus-visible { outline-color: var(--focus-accent-strong); }
}
```
Make `--focus-accent` a token that is WCAG-checked across themes.
Dylan: also add an accessible name to every icon-only button. aria-label must be explicit (not inferred). we have a couple using `title` only which isn't reliable for screen readers.
Ravi: found two instances: rotate-key and quick-logs were missing aria-label, relying on tooltip.
Nora: small accessibility nit: tooltips should not be the only accessible name. and prefer `aria-label` or visible text when space permits.
Priya: for contrast of icon glyph itself, we can switch to using currentColor and set color tokens per state. ensure hover/active tokens meet 3:1 against background. add a unit test in the design token test suite that computes contrast ratios for each token pair used in toolbar.
Dylan: let's also address keyboard target size — 24px icons with 8px padding reduce clickable area for touch. for keyboard users it's fine but we should ensure hit target >= 44px when possible or provide an expanded hitbox (visual compactness but larger target).
Ravi: i prototyped changes: increased focus outline to 3px, added aria-labels, adjusted hover color to #374151 in light theme and #d1d5db in dark theme. quick manual tests show improved visibility and passes 3:1 for those combos.
Nora: nice. can you open a PR with CSS + small markup change for aria-label? include screenshots before/after for light/dark and a screenshot of keyboard focus ring.
Ravi: will do. milestone: include in next patch (non-breaking). adding checklist: aria-labels added, focus-visible rules, token update, token tests.
Priya: once PR is up i'll run with VoiceOver and NVDA and check high-contrast mode (Windows HC theme).
Dylan: also add a short line in the Console style guide about icon-only controls: "always provide accessible name and visible focus that meets 3:1 contrast".
Nora: agree. small copy tweak suggestion for aria-label phrasing sample: `aria-label="Deploy model"` instead of `aria-label="Deploy"` when context helps, prefer explicitness.
Ravi: PR opened: #1482. assigned to @Ravi, reviewers @Nora and @Priya. includes token updates + tests.
a11y-bot: added card "compact toolbar: icon contrast & focus-visible" to board `a11y-tasks` with priority `medium`. automated accessibility checks queued for PR #1482.
Priya: thanks team. i'll post results of high-contrast testing here once complete.
Dylan: thanks — small changes but very big UX win. :rocket:
